title: QuickChain: response choreography scratchpad
content:
Goal
---
Sketch a lightweight feature for composing multiple response steps (chains) inside a single user-facing reply, with the ability to trade off fidelity, cost, and latency per segment. Useful for: concise answers + optional deeper read, inline citations followed by a short extract, or an immediate cheap summary with an async higher-fidelity expansion.

Why we care
- Customers want predictable unit economics without losing the ability to surface high-value text (e.g., code snippets, step-by-step).
- Avoid full high-tier model inference for every turn; can run cheap model for first-pass and conditionally escalate.
- Makes fallbacks and canary rollouts more graceful: chain can degrade last segment instead of whole response.

High-level idea
- A "QuickChain" response is composed of 1..N segments. Each segment has: intent label (e.g., summary, citation-extract, example), model tier (cheap/medium/high), token budget, SLO target.
- Runtime executes segments sequentially or in parallel depending on policy. Segments can be gated by earlier outputs (confidence, length, user click).
- API surface: user-facing param like "quickchain: true" or structured segments in the request body. We provide helper builders in SDKs.

Minimal PRD outline (very rough)
- Who: product teams building assistants, search summarizers, knowledge UIs.
- What: structured response composition that can mix two model tiers with gating predicates.
- Where: hosted API + Dedicated (initially hosted only).
- Success metrics: reduce P50 token cost per session by >=15% on targeted flows while keeping quality degradation (human eval score) <5% for top intents.

User stories
- As a growth app, I want short answers to return near instantly using small models, with an optional in-place "expand" that runs a higher-quality chain segment when the user taps "more".
- As an enterprise admin, I want to pin certain segments (citation extraction) to private models for compliance while using cheaper public models for summarization.
- As a product engineer, I want deterministic fallback: if high-tier segment fails, return earlier segments plus a fallback note instead of an error.

Example proto request (sketch)
- body: { prompt: "Explain X", quickchain: [ { label: "summary", model_hint: "gpt-medium", max_tokens: 120, gating: "always" }, { label: "examples", model_hint: "gpt-large", max_tokens: 200, gating: "on_click" } ] }
- Note: gating values can be always|on_click|conditional(confidence<0.6)|timebox

Runtime behaviour notes
- Default: run first segment (cheap) synchronously and stream to client. Mark subsequent segments as pending with ids for later retrieval.
- For conditional gating, run a fast classifier (cheap model) to decide if upscale is needed.
- Provide hooks in Console: per-route QuickChain hit rate, cost breakdown by segment label, breakouts for gated vs auto-upgraded segments.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Where to keep state for multi-step chains? Session store vs ephemeral IDs returned to client. (Prefer ephemeral chain id + storage TTL=24h)
- UX for clients: should we support auto-append when second segment completes (pushing to client) vs explicit client poll/click? Both—default: explicit unless route opts into auto-push.
- Pricing model: charge per-token per-segment as normal, but offer a specialized "chained response" metric to help customers understand unit economics.
- Latency implications for synchronous two-segment chains—how often will end-to-end p95 blow SLOs? Need empirical sims.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- SDK can declare a two-segment chain in request body and receive streaming summary for first segment + token-limited second segment retrieval API.
- Logging: each segment emits trace id, latency, tokens, model, and gating decision.
- Console: route-level visualization for chain composition and cost.
- Fallback: if second segment fails, API returns first segment + a standardized "expanded content unavailable" note and logs ticketable error.

Experiment plan
1) Internal A/B on a small set of flows (help center summarization, code explanation). Control: single high-fidelity call. Variant: QuickChain cheap-first + on-click upscale. Measure: cost/session, user click-to-expand rate, NPS proxy (short survey).
2) Canary on 5 customers opt-in for Dedicated. Track misclassification (gating false negatives), error modes, and rollback thresholds.

Instrumentation and metrics
- Chain hit rate (requests that used QuickChain)
- Segment success/failure rates
- Upscale rate (how often conditional gating triggered)
- Cost delta per session (median and 95th)
- Quality delta (human evals on sampled pairs)

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: users see degraded experience if gating misses high-value queries. Mitigate: conservative gating threshold + quick manual override route-level controls.
- Risk: complexity in billing & console confusion. Mitigate: explicit cost breakout by segment and a simple "estimated cost" flag returned in response metadata.

Next steps / TODOs
- Spike: simulate 100k sessions with synthetic prompts to estimate cost/latency distribution (owner: Mika).
- Draft CLI/SDK decorator for QuickChain (owner: Sam).
- Discuss pinning requirements with security (owner: Felicia) and add KMS notes if segments use different model infra.
- Write short proto Confluence page and link to JIRA INF-8793 for tracking.

Notes to self
- Keep initial surface as simple as possible (2 segments + declarative gating).
- Think about reusing existing prefix-caching and KV cache for second segment to avoid re-encoding.
- Consider a compact JSON manifest in response metadata so clients can render placeholders for pending segments.

Brain dump of UI microcopy
- "Loading more details…" vs "Expand for full explanation (cost may apply)"
- Should show an estimated cost delta when user hovers over "Expand"

End of scratchpad
summary: Scratchpad for QuickChain: structured, multi-segment response composition that trades fidelity vs cost and enables gated upscale. Contains PRD bullets, user stories, proto request sketches, acceptance criteria, open questions, experiment plan, and TODOs.
